title: Calcium meets fluoride
hook: Build a neutral combination, then double it.

knows: Ions have positive or negative charge.
doesNotKnow: How the simplest ion ratio makes an ionic compound electrically neutral.

misconception: Every ionic compound has one cation for each anion.
objective: Use ion charges to derive the smallest charge-neutral formula-unit ratio.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: An ionic formula unit contains Ca²⁺ and F⁻ ions. What is the smallest whole-number ratio of positive ions to negative ions that makes the total charge zero? One formula unit has 1 Ca²⁺ and 2 F⁻: its positive and negative charges each have magnitude 2. The simplest ratio is 1 : 2, written CaF₂. A real ionic solid is an extended lattice, not isolated molecules.
claims.source: Balance the charges and reduce the ratio; OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/2-6-ionic-and-molecular-compounds

claims.text: The circles depict ion counts rather than the real arrangement of an ionic lattice.
Recall: If every ion count in a neutral CaF₂ formula unit is doubled, what happens to the total charge? Doubling both positive and negative charges preserves their balance.
claims.source: Doubling zero total charge leaves zero.

recall.question: If every ion count in a neutral CaF₂ formula unit is doubled, what happens to the total charge?
recall.why: Doubling both positive and negative charges preserves their balance.
